about: THE RULES OF A VOYAGE - the crew's keep and pay, their stores, and what the sea does to them. A table the game reads (edit freely; every number is a STARTING GUESS TO TUNE). Food and drink are goods bought in the market (the Provisions and Food goods named below) and carried in the hold; water is put aboard free in any port (wells, springs, the river). A day's ration follows the monastic and military rations of the time: about a kilo and a half of bread a day was a labourer's (Frankfurt 794 fixes 12 two-pound loaves at a denier), with ale or water to drink.

crew._men: the Gislinge boat's crew (the user's decision, 2026-10-01)
crew._pay: deniers a man is owed each day aboard, paid out in port (the same as the world's crews)
crew._leave: a man owed this many days' pay may go ashore for good at the next port

rations._food: kg of food a man eats a day: bread, cheese, dried fish, salt meat
rations._drink: litres a man drinks a day: water, ale

water._weight: water counts against the hold like any cargo

health._hunger: health lost each day with no food
health._thirst: health lost each day with nothing to drink
health._recover: health regained each day fed and watered
health._seasick: waves (real metres) above which the men start to be seasick
health._seasick_cost: morale lost each day of rough sea, less as they get their sea legs
health._legs: days at sea after which seasickness is mostly gone (it returns after long ashore)

morale._unpaid: morale lost each day pay is owed past a week

aground._about: When she sticks fast on the way (the crew try the oars by themselves first), you choose how to get her off: wait for the tide (time runs fast until it floats her; only where a tide will), row her off, or over the side and push her to the nearest water deep enough. Graph: 'Aground - getting her off'.
aground._offer: game minutes stuck fast before the choice comes
aground._again: game minutes after 'leave her for now' (or a try that failed) before it comes again
aground._look: how far ahead the tide is looked at: a tide that floats her within this many game hours can be waited for
aground._rate: game seconds per real second while you wait for the tide (3600: an hour a second)
aground._row: game minutes the crew row hard before they give it up
aground._reach: how far the crew can push or haul her, in her own lengths
aground._speed: metres a second they move her, walking her through the shallows
aground._depth: the water they take her to: this times the water she needs
aground._push: the crew in the water: wet, cold, tired
aground._cold: more, in the cold months (November to March)
